title: Standing on FURM ground - A framework for evaluating Fair, Useful, and Reliable AI Models in healthcare systems

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the representativeness of training and deployment data (e.g., identifying majority-white populations) and stratifying model input features, output probabilities, and predicted labels by race and ethnicity to track disparate impacts and ensure adequate power to detect harms in minoritized groups.
Assessing the model's goal and ability to decrease missed diagnoses in non-male patients, and stratifying model outputs and performance tracking by sex.
Stratifying model input features, raw probabilistic outputs, and thresholded predictions by age group during post-deployment monitoring.

Conducting qualitative ethical reviews to determine if model predictions (e.g., trained on emergency department presentations) disproportionately direct clinical resources to patients with a higher baseline propensity to seek care, thereby exacerbating health disparities.
